newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's bourse ends week 0.43 pct lower.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's bourse ends week 0.43 pct lower.

text.p: The stock exchange closed 0.43 percent lower on Friday with privatisation bonds accounting for most of the trade during the week, stockbrokers said.
The bourse all-share index closed at 638.40 points against 641.16 points last Friday.
"A good number of privatisation bond holders who had not converted their bonds for the flotation of Imiter silver mine sold them during the week," a Casablanca-based broker said.
Second tranche bonds, issued in May 1996, fell to 1,146 from 1,240 dirhams last Friday. They give holders preferential options on equity in privatised firms.
Blue-chip banks such as Banque Commerciale du Maroc closed at 850 dirhams from 869 dirhams. Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur closed unchanged at 600 dirhams.
Conglomerate, ONA Group closed at 778 dirhams from 776 dirhams.
Ste Nationale d'Investissement closed at 713 dirhams from 725 dirhams.
In the energy sector, oil refinery Samir closed at 341 dirhams from 350 dirhams.
Steel mill Sonasid remained unchanged at 550 dirhams.
Credit firm Credor rose three dirhams to 755 dirhams Maroc Leasing edged up one dirham to 416 dirhams. Portfolio firm Financiere Diwan was unchanged at 333 dirhams.
Total trade on the official market was 27 million from 40.6 million dirhams.
On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 26.1 million from 48.9 million dirhams.
